utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis. With me today is the final member of our trial team, Mr. Neuner, and we're assisted today by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, my learned friends. Good afternoon to all in the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, with our assistants, Lejla Gluhic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And before we call the witness in, there's just one little point that the Trial Chamber would like to raise. It's a pity that it's a bit late, but this relates to the witness Berislav Marijanovic. He was cross-examined by you, Mr. Robson. You put to him a second statement that he was supposed to have made to an NGO somewhere. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The Commission for the Verification of War Crimes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he denied ever making that statement; am I right? He denied knowledge of that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my recollection of the evidence, and of course I'd have to check the transcript to be exact, but my recollection was that initially he did not recall giving a statement, but then later on, under cross-examination, he accepted that he did give that statement, because he accepted that the person who took the statement or the officers who took the statement must have spoken to him to put that information within the statement itself. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's not sort of spend more time on our recollections, but let me just double-check with you that this is the statement that is supposed to have been taken over from the (redacted) (redacted), is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I recollect the second statement was the statement taken by the Commission for the Verification of War Crimes in the Territory of the Croation Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and I believe that commission is based in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have two statements, the one that was used by the Prosecution and the other that is said to have been -- this document has been taken over from the (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: (redacted). I'm advised that this discussion actually took place in private session, so maybe we should go into private session. May the Registrar please put us into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Osman Fusko, and my colleague, Mr. Neuner, will be leading this witness in direct examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You didn't have any interest in that discussion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Fusko. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is your name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Osman Fusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in 1992, you were commanding an independent company belonging to the Mehurici Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in November 1992, you joined the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Esad Sipic. If I could ask that document PT1096 please be shown. Document dating from 14 May 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll repeat my question. My mic was off. I thought shouldn't you lay a basis for that exhibit before you ask for it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document which is from the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't you establish that through the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you seen in your time at this 306th Mountain Brigade, documents from that brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Not all the documents were available to me. I did see some, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You just spoke about Esad Sipic. Did you ever see a signature of Mr. Esad Sipic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I did, yes. I used to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I showed you a document bearing his signature, would you be in a position to recognise his signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I now may ask that the document PT1096 be shown to this witness, or should I ask further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: While the document is appearing on the screen, can I ask you where was the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade located in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: At what moment? At the moment when this document was issued? At that time, the battalion was billeted in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look, and if the original could be scrolled down a little bit, at the signature now. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Esad Sipic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on the very last line, or actually on this third-last line of the text, it says: "1BB." Could you explain what that means or what that stands for, please?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And again for the record, this was located in Mehurici; yes?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that this document please be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the name of this document that we give this exhibit number, what is the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The ERN number is 0603-1363 -- sorry, 1303 to 1304. It's actually just -- I apologise. I'll read it again. It's a one-page document which has the ERN 0603-1303 only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And until March 1993, you were assistant commander for Security and Intelligence in the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Of the 2nd Battalion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where was this 2nd Battalion located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion was located in a village called Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in March 1993, what post did you take, what new post did you take?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: In March 1993, I was transferred to the 306th Mountain Brigade as a security officer. It was either in March or in April; I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in that post?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: You mean as a security officer? I stayed until March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you work at that time from March 1993 until 1995?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: You mean the location?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Where was your office?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: In Krpeljici and also in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was your superior as a security officer in the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: My immediate superior was Asim Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what were your duties in the Military Security Service?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I performed military police duties and staff security duties as a security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how many military police officers were in the 306th Brigade in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Around 20 or so. I can't give you the exact number because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how much staff at the Military Security Service of that brigade in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please name them?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Myself, Asim Delalic and Haris Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you would learn about crimes in the AOR of the 306th Brigade, what investigative steps were undertaken by the 306th Brigade Military Security Service?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: If we were to learn and if it was within our powers, obviously we would search for the perpetrators of whatever crime was committed, and I say "if."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt? You just said "and I say 'if'." My question do you is: Did you learn about crimes committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did you do, in terms of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We couldn't do anything because the perpetrators were the Mujahedin, so we couldn't investigate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, Witness. You said that investigation measures could be taken out. Were there any prevention measures in place? Were they provided for any prevention measures to prevent possible crimes? Did you have those in place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, there was no way to prevent any crimes. The Mujahedin who were in the area were beyond anybody's control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. However, the measures of prevention, generally speaking, were they provided for at least on paper or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, as far as I know, there were no measures provided for in order to prevent the things that would eventually happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Neuner, to do this to you, but from the question that Judge asked, I have a question. When you say "the Mujahedin who were in the area wouldn't be under anybody's control," what do you mean by "anybody"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody could control them in whatever they were doing, in whatever tasks they had, if we may call those tasks. They did of their own initiative without any previous agreements with anybody. I don't know, to this very day, who was it who had sent them to that area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now when you say "anybody," do you mean anybody within your area of responsibility or the other two colleagues that you are talking about, or do you mean anybody in the world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mean the entire world, as the globe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you what do you mean by "anybody." Do you mean you and your colleagues within the 306th Mountain Brigade Security Services system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I meant. None of us could control them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The question from the Presiding Judge begs the question of: If you were aware of the Mujahedin having their own system of disciplinary investigations. So they -- My question really is: If they were not under your control, were they then under their own control, did the Mujahedin have their own military police who took care of investigations against crimes committed by members of Mujahedin? Just tell us if you know. If you don't know, then that's fine, but my question is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand the question, but I wouldn't be able to answer your question because it was impossible to establish any contacts with them at any time. In other words, I don't have any information as to whether they had any staff who were in charge of such tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. Sorry to do that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to start from what the Judges just asked. In 1992 and early 1993, where were the Mujahedin located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: They were located in the elementary school in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in that building, was there also another unit located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: You mean an army unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, there was the Sector Staff of Mehuric or the Regional Staff of Mehuric, but they were separated. The two were separated. The Regional Staff was on the second or the third floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where were the Mujahedin located in that building?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The third floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And there was one staircase or several staircases leading up that building?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: One staircase, one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to my learned friend. Page 12 of the transcript, lines 1 and 2, the witness didn't say that the Regional Staff was on the second or the third floor, but the other way around, that the Mujahedin were located there. The transcript has it that the Regional Staff was located there. I would like the witness to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Mujahedin were on the third floor, and the Regional Staff of Mehuric was on the ground floor of the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've got that now, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may ask, you said earlier there was also the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade located in Mehurici. You just talked about the Regional Staff earlier. Could you clarify at what point in time was one staff preceding or one unit preceding the other?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The Regional Staff of Mehuric was located in that school in Mehuric up to the moment when the 306th Brigade was established. When the 306th Mountain Brigade was established, only the battalion remained located in the elementary school in Mehuric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This was in November 1992 when the 306th Brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And within the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade, was there an assistant for military security?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Hasan Zukanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where was his office located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I don't know. Somewhere in the school. I really wouldn't be able to tell you where his office was within the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he in a position to send some information to you about the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: He was in a position to do that, but I never saw him sending any documents. If a document did arrive, it is possible that it reached the assistant commander for security directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 1st Battalion located in the school, the 1st Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Mirzet Ljubenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long did he stay in this position?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know, I wouldn't be able to give you a time frame. It was 12 or 13 years ago, so it's very difficult for me to remember details like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since we talked about the relationship of your service towards the Mujahedin, could I please show you a document, PT1092, dating 10th of May, 1993. The ERN number is 043-2452 to 2453. You see on the -- if you could scroll down, please, a little bit. You see this is a document which is sent to the General Staff of the ARBiH, but it also has a section about the 306th Mountain Brigade in it, and I'm interested, please, in the second page, where -- if it could please be scrolled up, yes -- where there is a text which is underlined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the second page in the English version, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it talks there about an undefined status of the Muslim forces from Mehuric that, and I quote: "... work on establishment of the 8th Muslim Brigade --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where are you quoting, sir? We would like --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is on the second line of page 2 of the English translation. Sorry, this is page 3 of the English translation. It says, "Forces from Mehuric" at the beginning on the first line and "Muslim" is on the second page actually of the English translation. "The Muslim forces from may reach that," and I'm quoting from the second line, "work from the establishment of the 8th Muslim Brigade and their fighters from our brigade that report to them." As I mentioned earlier, this is from -- under the heading of the 306th Mountain Brigade. Being in the Military Security Service at the time, Mr. Fusko, can you confirm that there were fighters from the 306th Brigade that went over to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, can I just establish one little point. Are you equating 8th Muslim Brigade with the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will ask a question about this in a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, then you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Should it be the other way around?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you are ahead of yourself, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm ahead of myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you everyone heard of the establishment of an 8th Muslim Brigade, Mr. Fusko?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let me start, then, earlier. The document talks about the undefined status of the Muslim forces from Mehurici. Who was meant with "The Muslim forces from Mehurici"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: In this document, it referred to the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the Muslim forces from Mehurici are the Mujahedin; yes?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I understand correctly, the document appears to suggest that fighters from "our brigade," meaning the 306th Brigade, report to them. Is that what you could also observe at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I did not see any reports on the part of the 306th Brigade fighters to the Mujahedin. At the end of the day, I could not observe them because the way they were billeted, there was no access.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could you please look at the document and observe that the Prosecution has asked two leading questions which I would kindly ask my learned friend not to do. Second of all, in this report, at least in the Bosnian language, there is no reference made that reports were sent to the 306th Brigade. It says "there are fighters from our brigade who apply to join them." This may be a mistake in translation. In any case, in my document I don't see a reference to any reporting. I would kindly ask my learned friend to read the document well before starting to put questions to the witness and check the translation, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, do you have any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The translation from the DVU Translation Service says you report to them, and we will verify whether this indeed should be translated differently, as my learned friend suggests.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you notice anybody who was applying to join the Mujahedin, as my learned colleague suggests the translation should read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, maybe we could verify another away. If you can ask the witness to read the relevant B/C/S portion and let the interpreter interpret for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Fusko, could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And let me say to you, where you are showing us the English version, the sentence starts with: "Forces from Mehurici," and I've been hearing you and the witness talk about Mujahedin forces. We haven't seen the first page to see whether the word before "forces" is "Mujahedin." Anyway, read the entire sentence, or rather get the witness to read the entire sentence in B/C/S and let's get an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have heard the suggestion from Your Honour. Could you please read the sentence, Mr. Fusko?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Can this be blown up a little? Thank you. "We have a lot of problems with the non-defined status of Muslim forces in Mehurici."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on, sir.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: "According to our information, they are currently --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please continue to read?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: --" ... they are currently working on the establishment of the 8th Muslim Brigade. Every day, fighters from our brigade apply to join either them or some other units. This interferes with our plans to use the units. This type of behaviour interferes with our plans. The social status of our fighters is very bad, and sometimes we are faced with ultimatums to provide them with the bare necessities that I have already informed you about."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will seek to alter the translation into the English language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And thank you to you, too, Madam Vidovic. You may proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please stay on the same page of that document, and the sentence in the original starts with: "Iz podataka." If you could read that out so that we get -- can get a translation.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Which sentence do you want me to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. On this page, the sentence starts with: "Iz podataka," four lines below the underlined sentences.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Very well: "We see from the information that so far not a single sentence has been pronounced in the valley. Being aware of the lack of efficiency of the judiciary, the fighters often break the law. We are daily involved in preventing leaks of confidential information."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This sentence, first of all, talks about the Biljani Valley. Could you explain to the Chamber what the Biljani Valley is?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: It's a region, it's the valley of the Bila River.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So this is where Mehurici is located?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which court in 1993 was competent to try cases from the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The court in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is that correct, from your perspective as a member of the Military Security Service, that not a single judgement or sentence has been passed with regard to that valley?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Well, up to the moment when the conflict broke out with the Croats, we did not have any problems. There were no criminal reports. But when it comes to the Mujahedin, we were not in a position to file any criminal reports because we could not corroborate such reports with any valid documents that would enable any court to receive such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. With regard to the 306th Brigade, Mountain Brigade, was there any judgement passed by May 1993 with regard to criminal offences by the court in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: There were no serious crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you, as a member of the Military Security Service of the 306th Brigade, say there were no serious crimes by May 1993 in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: As far as I know, before the outbreak of the conflicts with the Croats, we did not have any problems that would entice us to file criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in April 1993, at the end of April 1993, do you recall that there was a serious crime against Croats committed in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do you get that from, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And with regard to the Mujahedin, the second part of my question would be: Do you know whether any judgements or sentences have been passed with regard to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask to tender that document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT1092 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could it please be asked that the document PT1094 be shown to the witness. The ERN number is Y005-4266. This is a document from the 13th of May, 1993, type-signed by Mr. Asim Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could just ask you to look at the two underlined names, Ramo Durmis and Sljivo Malik which are mentioned here, and I will read the sentence out. It is the last paragraph, Your Honours, the third line -- fourth line of the English translation from above: "With the Mujahedin --" Sorry, I see I have a different version here. It's the second-last paragraph: "With the Mujahedin --" It's the third line from below: "With the Mujahedin are a sizeable number of Bosnians who are commanded by Ramo Durmis and Sljivo Malik, who studied in Saudi Arabia at one time, is with him." Could I ask you: Do you know who Ramo Durmis is?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I have heard of Ramo Durmis, and on one occasion I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: While I was passing through Mehurici, just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did you hear about Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I only heard that he was a member of the Mujahedin Unit, that he was up there with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So this means he stayed at the Mehurici school?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Not in the school in Mehurici, but in their camp in Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it says here in the sentence that Mr. Durmis commanded a sizeable number of Bosnians?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: How should I know whether he commanded or not? This is probably information obtained from the ground. Probably the information was obtained from the local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what do you know about Sljivo Malik?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I have heard of him, but I have never seen him and I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did you hear of him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Quite simply that he was also a member of that team, so to speak, those people who were with the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I ask that this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be exhibit number 136.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I just ask that Exhibit 92 be shown, page 13 of that Exhibit. The ERN number is 0471-7276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "Exhibit 92", it is Exhibit 92 in the record here, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Can I suggest that once a document has been admitted into evidence, we call it by the exhibit number and forget about ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just wanted to help my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For purposes of helping, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- the Registrar, because this document consists of several pages, and I'm only seek seeking to have the witness shown page 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please look at this picture, do you recognise anybody on this picture -- on these pictures?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: These people, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we start with the picture on top, sir.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we can start with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person who that is holding the microphone in the picture on top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know him personally. I probably saw him around. They all wore beards, and as far as I was concerned they were all Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please have page 4 shown from the same exhibit to the witness. ERN 0471-7266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do about the rest of the pictures on this page, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understood the witness that he doesn't recognise anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this person?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this person in 1992, towards the end, in the autumn, while they were still in Mehurici before they went to the camp, but that person didn't stay in Mehurici long. He soon disappeared. I don't know where he went off to, and I don't know what his name is, this one with the red beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where in Mehurici did you see him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I saw him in front of the school, going up to the third floor, where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And was he alone or accompanied by somebody?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Usually, the Arabs stuck together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So was he accompanied by somebody or not?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No, no. You mean someone among the Bosnian people?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In general. Was he alone or with others?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: They never walked around alone, not a single one of them. There were always two, three, or more of them together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Fusko, you said, at line 10 of page 24: "I saw him in front of the school going up to the third floor, where they were." And the question to you is: On that occasion when you saw him, was he alone or was he with somebody? Don't tell us what they used to do normally. Tell us what happened on that day. Was he alone or was he accompanied by somebody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in the company of his Arabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that help you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could please ask that Exhibit 90 be shown, a document dating 28th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Asim Delalic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the document talks about Mujahedin, led by Ramo Durmis, who reconnoitered the Probijeno Brdo sector, Elevation 1009, and that one person was killed in the conflict with the Frankopan Brigade. Do you know where the Probijeno Brdo sector is?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I was never there, but I do know where Probijeno Brdo is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask, please, that from the Court binder Map 9 is being shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're done with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we enlarge on your screen, and if you could please try to find Probijeno Brdo. And if the usher could, in a moment, assist the witness, please, in case he finds it. If the "stilo" could be passed to the witness, the "stilo."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see it here. Can we zoom in, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we enlarge it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [indicating]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could the "stilo" be given to the witness? Could you please encircle it and mark a "1" next to it? Could you mark a "1" next to it, please?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if the map could be lifted up a little bit, please, upwards. Okay, now it's -- okay. I think we have to do that, unfortunately, again. We can erase this. The witness is in a position to mark it again. May we please have also Mehurici displayed there? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, Witness, if you could please encircle again Probijeno Brdo and mark a "1" next to it.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know where the school in Mehurici as we talked about earlier?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle it and mark a "2" next to it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Next to Mehurici or next to the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Next to the school itself.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I can recognise the position of the school on this map, but approximately it could be around here [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a "2" next to it, please?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said that at some point in time, the Mujahedin moved out of the school. Do you know where they moved to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: They moved to Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you encircle with a "3" where the camp is -- or the location is where they moved to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know whether the camp was known by any name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since in the document we just saw there's reconnaissance going on in Probijeno Brdo sector, could you indicate who controlled -- the document was from the end of May. Who controlled, at the end of May, the territory between Probijeno Brdo and Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Between Probijeno Brdo and Mehurici, it should have been under the control of the 306th Mountain Brigade, but at that time there were no lines here or anything. This was done on their own initiative, if it has to do with a document you showed a bit earlier. The Mujahedin did this on their own initiative, going towards Probijeno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand, but the Frankopan Brigade mentioned in the document was obviously near that point, so I'm just asking you where were, so to speak, the ABiH or the other positions between --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have positions there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the end of May?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the end of May or, to enlarge the question, the beginning of June, did the ARBiH have any positions between Probijeno Brdo and Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What happened at the beginning of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Where do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In this area here we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: There was fighting in early June when there was a conflict between the Croats and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when this conflict began, where were the positions in this area being built?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I repeat, there were no positions here. They weren't set up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But if I understand you correctly, a conflict began. A conflict between whom?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Between the HVO and the armija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And from what positions, if any, were the Army BiH units starting when the conflict began in this area?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question because I was away from the area at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did you come back to the area?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I came back on the day when the conflict broke out. I left my house and went off towards Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at the time you went to Mehurici, what month was it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: It was June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in what part of June was it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The first half of June. I can't be precise about the date. The 8th, the 9th, maybe the 7th. I can't recall the date now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And around the 7th to the 9th of June, 1993, from where were the army units starting, in terms of the conflict you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, before you answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. This is the second time the same question is being put, where the unit started from. It's a very leading unit [sic], if they started out at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction "leading question."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is it's a leading question, sir. Any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned -- it's almost disappearing, page 21, line 3, that army BiH unit -- excuse me. Page 29, line 7, "On the day the conflict broke out," and my only question was: When the conflict broke out, and I understand it was between the ABiH and the HVO, from where were the forces coming so that the conflict could indeed break out?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me the same question, but I can't answer it because on that morning I was at home, coming back from the forward command post at Vlasic, and you could already hear shooting in the whole valley, so I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you came to Mehurici, were there any soldiers at the time in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: When I arrived in Mehurici, there were a few people in uniform belonging to the army of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And were they engaging in anything or they were just standing there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: They were just standing there. They weren't doing anything at that time. A few minutes or an hour or two later, Croat civilians began to arrive in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From what area?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: From the area of Puselje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object again. I think the question should be whether the witness knows from where these people arrived before asking them from where they came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying, Madam Vidovic, that if the witness doesn't know where they came, is it impossible for him just to answer, "I don't know where they came from"?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm objecting because today the questions have been highly leading. The witness is constantly being led, because when such questions are asked, "Where do they come from," the assumption is being made that the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I accept that there have been a number of leading questions today. I'm talking about this specific question, "Where did they come from? If you know, you tell. If you don't know, you say, "I don't know." Is that any clearer in any fair manner, ma'am, that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept what you say, but because there were two or three leading questions in a row, that's why I stood up. But of course the witness can answer as Your Honour said. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, sir, get the answer to the question, "Where did they come from?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The civilians who arrived in Mehurici, well, at the time of their arrival I didn't know where they were coming from. Later on, I learned they were from Puselje, Bikosi, Podstinje and so on, but mostly from those places, the area of Maline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please mark on the map in front of you the locations you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please for Podstinje, could you use the number 4? Just encircled --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness, for the record, has just encircled Gornje Maline and placed a "5" next to it. He's now encircling Bikosi, and he's placing a "6" into it. Do we have -- the witness is just encircling Puselje and is marking a "7" into it. Thank you. And where were you when you were seeing these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I was in the primary school in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did the persons who arrived there do?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: You're referring to the civilians who were arriving?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: They were accommodated in the gym of the primary school. But as to what they were doing, well, they were trying to survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And of what ethnicity were these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you talk to some of these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: My conversation was with a Dr. Puselja, a lady, and there was also a nurse whose name was Kata, I think, among them. So we discussed what the people needed, how they could be helped, but that was on the following days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you learn something in the conversations, what had happened to these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: As for what had happened to these people, what they said, although I myself did not talk to them, but I heard that they were saying that some people had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at what time of the day did you learn that information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon. I heard this from the Croat civilians who were talking among themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what exactly were they talking, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: That they were afraid of the Mujahedin, that that was the main reason for their arrival, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And with regard to the killed persons, what information could you learn?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I didn't learn any information, but later on there were rumours going round that at Bikosi people had been killed by Mujahedin or Arabs or whatever they referred to them as.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Did the civilian Croats who came to Mehurici, did they come walking on foot by themselves or were they brought there by someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certain came on their own and some came with members of the BiH Army because they were afraid of the Mujahedin. They felt that they could be protected by the army members. That's why they came with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is a bit unclear to me. You say that you observed civilian Croatians arriving at Mehurici, some of them being escorted by soldiers of the ABiH? Do you have any idea as to how this came about? Where did they meet these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I suppose that people started seeking shelter, and when they saw people from the BH Army, they joined them because of all that, because they had learned that the Mujahedin were on their way up there. And all they were saying was that they were afraid of the Mujahedin and that's why they had arrived in Mehuric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And so they would have contacted these ABiH soldiers at the places from which they fled and asked for protection and escort up to Mehurici; is that how I'm to understand what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And when they came to Mehurici, you told us that they were accommodated in the school of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the gym, in the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And offered food and clothes or protection simply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view of the things while I was there they had food, they had some other provisions, some mattresses and sleeping bags. It was the staff of the Civilian Protection in Mehuric who provided that. It was within their purview to organise all that. The people had food and shelter and everything. The truth is the gym is not the most comfortable of places. A gym is a gym. But in any case, they were safe there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately how many came over those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there were some 200 of them. I can't give you the exact number. Even if I'd known the number at the time, I wouldn't be able to recall it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Your answer is certainly sufficient. Thank you very much, sir. You may proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I've just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The people who came to your school, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And with regard to the people who were allegedly killed, was there any indications whether these people had been armed before they were killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If please the map could be captured and admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 137.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think this is also a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner. We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, you are left with just about 11 minutes or so from your estimated time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, I'm told 26. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I just want to ask you, the people where you heard who were killed, do you know what happened to them before they were killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know in which -- whether these people were also moving at the time and then got killed at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Rumours had it, although not correct, that they had been kidnapped by some members of the BiH army, that there was something to that effect going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the transcript, page 36, line 20, it says that the witness said that, "These people had been kidnapped by members of the army." The witness said that "They were kidnapped from." I hope that this is understood that it is self-explanatory, that they were not kidnapped by the army members but taken from the ranks of the army members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that what the BiH original was saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness can clarify. He said that they were kidnapped from the BiH army, and in the record it was recorded that they were kidnapped by the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word "snatched" or "kidnapped" means that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Means what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word "snatched" or "kidnapped" means -- should I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word I mentioned means this: Members of the army tried to protect them and take them to a safe place, and they were kidnapped by the Mujahedin, the Arabs, whatever you want to call them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: From that BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. They were not members of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You don't understand my question. Let's leave it. They were kidnapped -- [Microphone not activated]. You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you said members of the army tried to protect the persons before they were kidnapped. From which army unit were the members who tried to protect?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: We have just touched upon that question. As far as I know and as far as I heard, because I was not there to see those people with my own eyes, I believe they were members of the army from the 1st Battalion. This was never confirmed to me. At the end of the day, I was just an officer, and I was never in charge of any investigations. I never investigated the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And by "1st Battalion," you're referring to which brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which was based in Mehurici at the school?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion was in Mehuric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what did the soldiers who tried to protect the persons do after the kidnapping had happened?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I don't know. I never came in touch with these people. What I'm telling you now is what I heard, something that was never confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you try to verify this rumour or allegation?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: There was no way for me to verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the highest person at Mehurici school at the time -- military person at the time you learned that information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Those were all desk officers, because at the Command was split into three parts. There were no higher-ranking officers there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you seek to inform some superior away from the school about what you learned?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Well, only on the following day did the commander of the brigade arrive, and the assistant commander for security. At the moment when they arrived, I was standing in the corridor. I was talking to the assistant commander. I tried telling him. He told me that he also had heard that some crimes had heard that some crimes had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who is -- the assistant commander for security is Hasan Delalic you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, don't put the answer in the mouth of the witness. Ask him who the assistant for security was, don't tell him who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wanted to save time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've got to do the right thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Delalic coming alone?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was with him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: The brigade commander was with him on that day. It was one or two days after the outbreak of the conflict. On Day 1, they could not arrive. Nobody in their right mind would have risked their lives to face all that shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just captured, on page 39, line 8, the word "Hasan Delalic." Could you please state what the assistant for security of the 306th Brigade had for a name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Asim Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And until Mr. Delalic came to see you, did you have informed anybody about what you learned?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: There was nobody to inform. As I've already told you, the communication was down with the brigade. The brigade was split into three different parts in Krpeljici, Rudnik, one part in Mehuric, and the officers who happened to be at their own homes when the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you just said, on line 39 -- on page 39, line 5, that the assistant commander for security, Mr. Delalic, had already heard that some crimes had taken place. What did he tell you when he came?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I tried informing him that some crimes had happened in the zone of combat activities. He replied that he had also heard something to that effect, and he also told me that he still didn't know what exactly had happened, that it remained to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And about what type of crime had he heard?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: He heard of the crime, and he meant people who had been killed. When I say "people," I mean men, women. I don't know exactly who was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did he know or have indications by whom they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: He did not say anything about that at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about verifying the rumours?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: What time do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion between Mr. Delalic and the brigade commander about verifying the basis for these rumours that people had been killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: My conversation with the assistant commander was very short, and I never exchanged a word with the commander. I only greeted him. And I really don't know what kind of discussions they had afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you receive a particular instruction?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I did not receive any particular instructions with this regard. Delalic most probably took upon himself the responsibility of investigating, of looking into the matter, into seeing what had happened. I don't know what happened. He was the one with whom I left it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened to the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Again, I wouldn't be able to answer because I was not there, and second of all it was the Civilian Protection who were in charge of cleaning the terrain after such events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could the dead bodies not be an object of an investigation to find out about the rumours?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I repeat again, I can't answer your question. I don't have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you a document, PT number 1236, a telegram dating from the 12th of June. It says, on the first line, from the 306th Mountain Brigade for the 3rd Corps Command, and I just want to read this second -- the last two sentences to you: "There are indications of the execution of 20 captured civilians and (illegible) and members of the HVO." Does this sentence adequately reflect the view held within the Military Security Service of the 306th Brigade on the 12th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase or repeat your question? I didn't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I look at this sentence again, it talks about indications of an execution of 20 captured civilians and members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might ask, Mr. Neuner, is the number of the people killed in that incident not an agreed fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly it is, but what I'm trying to explore is that, yeah, the word "execution" is mentioned here, and this is so far also an important point, and it just reflects a contemporaneous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you trying to confirm whether they were executed and not killed; are you making a distinction between the two words?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not trying to make a distinction between it. I'm just asking the witness what he knows, since he was in the area and was also subject to these rumours, and I'm just asking him whether the content of the document is adequate as he received it at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's just my problem. This witness has just been telling us hearsay about this incident from the beginning of his testimony, and we've had people here who have testified who were on the scene. I'm not quite sure what it is you want from this witness, really. I've been sitting here the whole afternoon trying to find out why this witness was called, and I can't find it. I couldn't see it even in reading the statement. You know, now, you're taking time to find out whether 20 civilians and members of the HVO were executed, and I'm just wondering -- I'm trying to find out what is it on that point you want to find out, you want to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be removed for a second, please, before I give the answer? Does he read English? Does the witness read English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You should know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Under these circumstances, may I ask the witness to take the headphones down? Your Honours, late in October this witness has authored a document which is, to a certain extent, in contradiction to the text of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of the document which is in front of you right now. He has personally signed that document. And what I'm trying to find out, to explore, is whether the witness's knowledge back in June, directly after the events, like here on the 12th of June, might have been different so that he later changed, eventually, his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me find out, is this witness the author of this telegram?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There is another witness who will come who is the witness's superior, and he has met his superior, as we just heard, one or two days after the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the answer to my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He's not the author of it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- but he's part of the Military Security Service, which is, so to speak, involved in conducting measures or could be involved in conducting measures to find out and verify the rumours about what is going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's told you there's no way he could verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, but he might confirm that the content of that document is adequate because he at the time also heard the rumours, and that is all that I'm trying to establish; the basis of what he knew in June, and later on try to ask him why he changed his mind in October. That is all that I'm trying to establish, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just add, then, before the witness takes on his earphones, that if anything here is interesting, it should be the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was coming to the last sentence as well, but I thought there are one or two words in the first statement which I tried to explore with this witness first, and I will come then very quickly to the second -- to the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will try to make it brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, my first question is: Having just read this sentence for you, does this -- does the fact -- is that a correct description in this document that on the 12th of June, indications of an execution of about 20 persons existed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: First of all, I did not see this document. Second of all, we heard from the people who had crossed over. This was the main indication. Later on, it turned out that they had been executed by the Mujahedin and that no members of the army took part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. But in essence, whoever was executing these men, it turned out that they had been executed; is that what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Whether they were executed or how they were killed, it all boils down to the fact that they were killed, they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the sentence also mentioned that the 20 persons were captured, so captured persons had been executed. Were these the indications you had or you heard at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: I heard nothing of any prisoners. I only heard later on that some Croats had been kidnapped, but I don't think that they were ever imprisoned, they were ever turned into prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then the next sentence says that an investigation is pending on the 12th of June because the document dates from the 12th of June. Do you know that an investigation was pending at that time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: After the events, Asim Delalic took all that upon himself, and he was the one who pursued the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were not involved?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to the next document. The PT number is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, before we let this document go, I did not fully understand who sent the telegram and who was it addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I read this in the record, Your Honours. It says, in the very first line, that it's sent from the 306th Brigade to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 306th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But we have no indication of who in the 306th Mountain Brigade, who actually sent it. I mean, the witness says he doesn't know anything of this telegram, and I'm just trying to ascertain --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness has confirmed that Mr. Delalic may have been or was involved in the investigation, and he has also talked about the fact that an execution may have occurred, according to the rumours, and instead of the word "captured" he said"kidnapped."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't it then better to ask Mr. Delalic about this document rather than ask the witness who knows nothing about it? And you're saying this telegram was from the 306th Mountain Brigade, and it was going to the 3rd Corps. Why is it that the conclusion, where the seal is -- or that's the seal of the recipient. Okay, I can see that. That's fine. But my first question then stands. Isn't the appropriate witness to deal with this document the person who was involved in investigations, Mr. Delalic rather than this witness, who has told you several times this afternoon that he was not involved in investigations?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment to confer, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please ask that the witness takes off his headphones again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, will you please take off your headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Delalic will indeed talk about this document when he later comes, but in October this very witness is authoring a document which, so to speak, is authored for Mr. Delalic, and both men were, so to speak, working close together. And therefore they're talking -- this witness will talk, in this October document, about the investigation in its entirety and about the result itself. So one cannot assess the weight of the one document by seeing the other in combination with it, and I'm just trying to get this witness's opinion about both documents so that Your Honours can assess it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, sir, this witness has told you this afternoon, when you put this document on the screen, that he has never seen this document before. Isn't it therefore appropriate to ask this witness about what he authored in October --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will do so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- and then ask Mr. Delalic, when he comes, to reconcile what he instructed this witness to write in October with what he received here, if this was received by Mr. Delalic? This witness -- you're asking this witness to do something to a document he knows absolutely nothing about. He's seeing this document for the first time today. That's his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have shown this witness the document on occasion of his statements, and he has made some comments about it, and we have -- I tried to explore certain things about the document, and I believe the witness has confirmed certain parts of it. I was already moving on to the next document. I'm two documents away from being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't dispute that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I wasn't trying to go back to this document, Your Honour. I'm prepared to proceed as you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Understand though, sir, that the Trial Chamber is faced, once it gets out of this court, with making sense of what this document is in relation to this witness, and if we can't see that sense now, we are likely never going to see it later. Now, notwithstanding your explanations, I still don't see the sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm prepared to proceed, to conclude soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I don't mean to interfere with what you are leading, but I would like to follow what you are saying and what you are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I at least ask that the document is marked for identification, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. May the document be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification MFI 138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is PT1443, dating from 3 of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say "PT1" --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: "... 443". The document refers to a visit of Mr. Merdan and Father Stjepan in paragraph 1 of it, and Mr. Fusko is referred to in paragraph 4(a) of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, the last exhibit, PT1584 is being shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature, Mr. Fusko?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're sending this document to the 3rd Corps and the Operations Group Bosanska Krajina, the military security organs there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you explain how you came to draft that document?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
utterances.text: This document was draft pursuant to a request that had to have been sent to us. I consulted with Asim Delalic. I asked him what we were supposed to do. He told me to draft a report; i.e., information to say that the BiH Army had not committed any criminal offences, that nothing of the sort had been done by members of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that fair to say that you received an instruction to put that information in?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN FUSKO
